analysis.topic_title: Python IndexError: list index out of range
analysis.praise: You found the fix yourself, and you sensed the loop runs too far.

concepts.label: Loop runs one step too far
concepts.expected_idea: range(len(nums) + 1) produces 0, 1, 2, 3, so the loop tries one index more than exists.
concepts.evidence_quote: I think the loop runs too many times.
concepts.reason: Correct direction, but you didn't say which i causes the problem.

concepts.label: Indexes start at 0
concepts.expected_idea: Valid indexes are 0 to len - 1, so a 3-item list has no index 3.
concepts.reason: Zero-based indexing, the real rule here, isn't mentioned.

concepts.label: Reading doesn't empty the list
concepts.expected_idea: print(nums[i]) only reads; the list keeps all 3 items. The error is a missing index, not an empty list.
concepts.evidence_quote: By the end the list becomes empty
concepts.reason: Reading items does not remove them; the list never becomes empty here.

concepts.label: Correct fix
concepts.expected_idea: Use range(len(nums)) or loop directly with for n in nums.
concepts.evidence_quote: I removed the +1 and it worked

lessons.title: Reading never removes items
lessons.core_idea: nums[i] just looks at an item, like reading a page number. The list still has 4, 8, 15 at the end. Python crashed because it was asked for a position that doesn't exist.
lessons.example: Reading a classmate's name from the register doesn't remove them from the class.
lessons.you_said: The list becomes empty by the end of the loop.
lessons.actually: The list is unchanged; the code asked for index 3, which doesn't exist.
lessons.check_yourself: Which list methods actually remove items?

lessons.title: Counting starts at 0
lessons.core_idea: Python numbers positions from 0. A list with 3 items has positions 0, 1, 2. The last valid index is always len(list) - 1.
lessons.example: In a 3-floor building numbered from the ground floor as 0, the floors are 0, 1, 2; there is no floor 3.
lessons.you_said: You didn't mention how indexes are numbered.
lessons.check_yourself: What is the last index of a 10-item list?

lessons.title: The extra step is i = 3
lessons.core_idea: range(n) gives 0 up to n - 1. So range(len(nums) + 1) = range(4) gives 0, 1, 2, 3. The last value, i = 3, asks for nums[3], and that triggers the IndexError.
lessons.example: range(4) → 0, 1, 2, 3: four numbers, but your list has only three slots.
lessons.you_said: The loop runs too many times.
lessons.actually: It runs exactly once too many, and i = 3 is the bad index.

code_fix.explanation: Looping over items directly can never go past the end.
